intent: Revert the sensor row to the best-raced layout: five sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.04, 16 mm footprint. Keep wheels, body and mass unchanged. The aim is to recover the iteration 3 result (69.46) by holding geometry and letting the Integrator restore kp 1.2. I am not repeating the ±0.04 row yet, because the iteration 4 result (61.49) is the first evidence against it, and it was confounded with a gain change. If the controller returns to kp 1.2 and the score stays below 69, the geometry is not the cause and the next test should be the controller's start-up or entry gain.
learning: Open hypotheses: (1) the ±0.04 row was worse because the lower kp (1.0) slowed the response, not because of coverage, so I will test the row again only with kp 1.2; (2) line loss at 1.0 events per run may come from the start of the course or from entry speed rather than from the row edge, since widening the row did not remove it; (3) the 16 mm footprint may add edge noise, which would raise oscillation on the s-bend. Please report, in the integration feedback, the progress at the first line-loss event on each track and the max error at that moment, and whether the loss occurs at the start. That will show whether the remaining line loss is a coverage problem or a control problem.
rationale: Iteration 4 scored 61.49, down from 69.46 at iteration 3. The only geometry change was widening the row from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m at 16 mm. Progress fell on the s-bend (0.210 to 0.160) and oval (0.184 to 0.170), and line loss stayed at 1.0 events per run on every track. Max error still reached about 0.062 m, so the 0.06 m off-track limit remains the binding failure. Two things changed together: the row widened and the Integrator lowered kp from 1.2 to 1.0. S-bend oscillation fell from 0.168 to 0.142, which fits a lower steering gain, but the lower gain also appears to have slowed progress. I cannot separate the geometry effect from the gain effect, but the wider row did not produce the line-loss improvement I predicted: line loss did not fall below one event per run. Because the only geometry that has produced the best score is ±0.03 m at 16 mm, I am reverting to that geometry. The reach from that row (about 0.0505 m) is still the best measured result. I am not repeating the ±0.04 row until a race isolates it at kp 1.2. I did not take the Integrator's advice to hold the ±0.04 row, because its own kp change was part of the candidate and the result is worse. Expected result: a score near 69 if the kp 1.2 controller is restored, and no change in geometry from the best raced design. I am not committing to a forward offset, since slalom oscillation was 0.147 and below the 0.15 trigger.
